about: The PKPR keypad's rule (specs/hex-keypad HK-R2, HK-R5, HK-R7): for the text typed and the PKPRs in stock, the keys that can come next (in keypad order, 1234567890abcdef), the PKPRs that match (stock order, each once) and the one left when exactly one matches. Hand-written; mazama_core's hex_keypad tests and the phone's hex_keypad tests both run every case.

cases.why: nothing typed: every character that appears in any PKPR, in keypad order
a match anywhere, not only at the start: '1' is inside ab12c
two PKPRs share 'a': both match, and the keys are what follows 'a' in either
the last character of a PKPR: it matches, and no key follows
the whole hex part typed: still the one match
a typed 'pkpr-' prefix, any case, and surrounding space don't count
stock in upper case and without the prefix matches the same way
nothing in stock has it: no keys, no matches
a character no PKPR's hex part holds
no stock: no keys, no matches
the same PKPR listed twice (one row per lot) is one match
one PKPR inside another: both match, so none is the only one, and the longer one's next key is lit
a repeated character: the key is lit where the text appears again later in the PKPR
